rows.paragraph: We first prove the finiteness facts used below. A subgroup of a finite-rank free abelian group is free of finite rank. In the proof of Lemma 5.1 of the included Thom/Euler chapter, restrict its well-ordered basis to the finitely many original basis elements. At each coordinate the quotient subgroup embeds in the original copy of \(\mathbb Z\), and is either zero or generated by a least positive integer. A chosen lift adds at most one basis vector. The resulting basis has at most the original rank. A subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finitely generated: pull it back under a surjection from a finite-rank free group, use the preceding statement, then take its image. Quotients and finite extensions are finitely generated as well. For an extension, lift a finite generating set of its quotient and adjoin a finite generating set of its kernel; subtracting a lifted expression puts each original element in the kernel.
